integrity: For omitted crown vertices, identifying sets are exactly the selected opposite part with the matched endpoint removed. This gives the solid omission rule plus two domination boundary families. The stronger self-location condition forces all omissions to one side unless exactly one matched pair is omitted. These classifications yield both polynomials and basis counts directly.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns connected crown graphs with n at least three.
It treats self- and solid-locating-dominating codes, not ordinary locating domination or identifying codes.
Finite exhaustive verification through n=8 is corroborative only.
A differently phrased or non-indexed crown result may exist.
title: Self- and solid-locating-dominating code polynomials of crown graphs
